architecture.fell_back_and_why: Ran in MODE-OFF exactly as the meta-agent specifies when --sync is absent: no snapshot pinned, no active_snapshot written, every stage read the live tree at --target_root, and the tree was treated as read-only throughout (the caller forbade modification, and mantis-patch is the only stage that would have written to it). The target has no VCS (git rev-parse fails), so SNAPSHOT_ID would have been the content: tier and Stage 0 (mantis-history) had no history to mine. Stage 0.5 (mantis-structural-index) was skipped because the toolkit ships the contract but not workspace/helpers/query_structural_index.py, and the skill declares the index HINT-only with a documented grep fallback; discovery therefore ran on exhaustive reads plus grep, which is the skill's own floor. Stages 1-4 (summarize / architecture / threat-model / plan) were not materialized as separate KB artifacts: on a 57-file, ~4,800-line target the supervisor folded the partition map, trust boundaries and per-partition attacker model directly into the researcher dispatch prompts rather than writing workspace/kb/*.md that only this run would read. That is a real deviation, recorded here rather than papered over with after-the-fact KB files. Stage 5 (researcher) ran as the skill's wave-based swarm, but with waves of at most four sub-agents instead of the skill's suggested 10-20 Wave-1 triage agents, per the caller's concurrency cap. sitewatch-desktop was audited by the supervisor in its own context instead of a sixth sub-agent, because the wave slots were full and the partition was small; it was then handed to an independent reviewer like every other partition. Stages 6 (dedupe), 10 (chain), 12 (calibrate) and 14 (report) were executed by the supervisor in this context: with 41 findings across six disjoint partitions there were no cross-file duplicates to merge, chains were recorded inside the impact and scope fields of the findings that compose them rather than as separate Super Findings, and the report was emitted in the caller's JSON contract instead of MANTIS's markdown review packet. Stage 9 (reproduce) and Stage 11 (patch) were skipped outright: no runtime, no build toolchain for Swift/Go/Node/Python in this environment, and patching would have written to a target the caller declared read-only. Every finding is therefore static-evidence only; none carries a executed proof-of-concept, and the two findings that most depend on out-of-tree behaviour are marked probable rather than confirmed. Stage 13 (reflect) had no per-subagent transcript paths exposed by this harness, so it was recorded as a missing-transcript skip per the skill's own instruction rather than silently emitting zero learnings.

findings.title: Caller role is overwritten by the client-supplied x-catalog-role metadata header (privilege escalation to admin)
findings.class: CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision / privilege escalation
findings.impact: Any holder of a valid session token - including the lowest-privilege read-only account - adds the metadata pair `x-catalog-role: admin` to any request and becomes an admin for that call: DeleteItem on any row in the tenant (server.go:148-156), and publishing items as VISIBILITY_PUBLIC via CreateItem/UpdateItem (server.go:87, 122). findings.recommendation: Remove the override, or treat the header as a request to *narrow* privilege rather than set it: keep the session role authoritative and accept x-catalog-role only when the requested role is a member of the session's own role set (which requires the sessions table to store a role list and Session to expose it). Also add x-catalog-role to gateway strippedHeaders so a downgrade of the interceptor cannot be driven from the public HTTP port.

ParseFilter/ParseOrderBy - the allowlisting parsers that make the Search path safe (search.go:39-91, used at server.go:180-187) - are never called on the export path, even though the file's own header comment claims `every literal becomes a bound parameter rather than text in the statement` (search.go:14-15).

findings.title: Node bootstrap silently re-enables docker privileged mode and host volume mounts on every fleet node, overriding the hardened client baseline

Prefer Nomad `host_volume` declarations (already used at nomad-client.hcl:8-11) over `volumes.enabled = true`, and keep `allow_privileged = false` everywhere else.

findings.title: The /auth router bypasses the fleet-auth middleware yet reaches the same licensing-api upstream, letting an unauthenticated client supply the X-Fleet-Role/Tenant/Subject identity headers the upstream trusts

config/gateway-routes.yaml:17-24 - same host, same backing service as the protected router, but the auth middleware is dropped:
  17	    licensing-auth:
  18	      rule: "Host(`licensing.council.gov.example`) && PathPrefix(`/auth`)"
  19	      entryPoints: ["websecure"]
  20	      service: licensing-api
  21	      middlewares:
  22	        - compress

versus the protected sibling, :6-13:
   6	    licensing-api:
   7	      rule: "Host(`licensing.council.gov.example`) && PathPrefix(`/api`)"
   9	      service: licensing-api
  11	        - fleet-auth

and the contract the upstream relies on, :37-46:
  37	    # The auth sidecar resolves the caller's session and hands back the role and
  38	    # tenant it belongs to, which upstreams read instead of re-parsing the token.
  39	    fleet-auth:
  40	      forwardAuth:
  43	        authResponseHeaders:
  44	          - "X-Fleet-Role"
  45	          - "X-Fleet-Tenant"
  46	          - "X-Fleet-Subject"

authResponseHeaders overwrites those three headers only on routers that run fleet-auth. On the /auth router nothing strips or overwrites them, so whatever the client sends arrives at http://licensing-api.service.consul:8080 (:70) unchanged.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated caller on the internet sends `GET https://licensing.council.gov.example/auth/... ` with `X-Fleet-Role: admin`, `X-Fleet-Tenant: <victim>`, `X-Fleet-Subject: <victim>` and reaches the same licensing-api process that, per the file's own comment at :37-38, reads those headers instead of re-parsing the token. Anything the service exposes under /auth that acts on caller identity (session exchange, tenant switch, token mint) is then executed as the forged identity, giving cross-tenant access in a multi-tenant licensing API. It also poisons the audit trail: the gateway keeps exactly these two headers in the access log (jobs/edge-gateway.nomad.hcl:59-60) and vector ships them to the shared bucket, so forged tenant/subject values are recorded as fact.
findings.recommendation: Add a headers middleware to every entrypoint that unconditionally removes X-Fleet-Role/X-Fleet-Tenant/X-Fleet-Subject from inbound requests (customRequestHeaders with empty values), applied before any router, so the only source of those headers is the forwardAuth response. Attach it to licensing-auth as well, and treat the headers as advisory in the upstream rather than as the authorization decision.

Attacker = an unauthenticated client on the internet. No test/dev naming; the route is on the production public host.

No hardcoded secret.

   4	  type        = "system"
  46	        mount {
  47	          type     = "bind"
  48	          source   = "/var/lib/nomad/alloc"
  49	          target   = "/var/lib/nomad/alloc"
  50	          readonly = true
  51	        }

  10	include = ["/var/lib/nomad/alloc/*/traefik/local/access.log"]

  65	        destination = "secrets/pg.env"
  66	        env         = true
  69	POSTGRES_PASSWORD={{ .Data.data.superuser_password }}

  68	        perms       = "0644"

findings.title: Drained settlement notices are never marked processed, so every notice is re-posted every five minutes for two days
findings.class: Broken idempotency on a financial write path (CWE-837 / duplicate ledger postings)
findings.evidence:
flows/ingest.py:50-60 selects by time window only, with no processed/consumed predicate:
  52:             SELECT idempotency_key, tenant_id::text, source, payload
  53:             FROM ingest_events
  54:             WHERE received_at > now() - interval '2 days'
  55:             ORDER BY received_at ASC
  56:             LIMIT %s
and the flow never marks anything, it just posts with a brand-new batch id each pass:
  91:         posted += post_batch(settings.dsn, tenant, str(uuid.uuid4()), accepted)
The table has no state column to mark - tasks/postings.py:28-34 declares only (idempotency_key, tenant_id, source, payload, received_at) - and a grep for UPDATE/DELETE/processed over the whole partition returns nothing. The deployment runs on a 300-second interval: prefect.yaml:58-59
  58:     schedule:
  59:       interval: 300
The idempotency key only de-duplicates the EVENT row (ingest.py:33-34 `ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING`), never the posting.
findings.impact: Every settlement notice is posted again on each five-minute run for the whole 48-hour window - roughly 576 duplicate posting batches per notice - each with a fresh batch_id (uuid4 at line 91), so nothing downstream can collapse them: batch_totals (postings.py:122-134) groups by batch_id and reports each duplicate as a clean new batch. A partner therefore gets its chosen amounts multiplied into the ledger ~576x for free, and the nightly reconciliation the flow exists to relieve is fed corrupted balances. The control that was supposed to prevent this (the partner's idempotency key) is applied one layer too early.
